items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: I talked to Dave before I left, at Dave's Fifth Avenue. And I said, 'Dave, I know I can get a group out here,' and I was telling him about my brother and so-and-so.

ctx.x: Musically, I wasn't satisfied with working in the New Washington Hotel, playing 'Tea for Two' and all that. And we had to play dressed in tuxedos and bow ties and play 'Tea for Two.' I wasn't too thrilled about that. That wasn't playing, to me. We were answering requests and all. The tunes were OK, some of the tunes were OK, but it just wasn't hardcore jazz playing.

I wanted to hear the drums and some horns and all that. So it didn't take much for the newness to wear off of that. I felt very bad because I thought that's what I was going to do. And I felt bad because, well, I made another stupid move, I'm thinking in my mind, and I need to get out of here. And that was...Meantime, I'd gone to Dave's Fifth Avenue...
